words.eg: That is the best {advice} anyone gave me before moving.

no.an advice|advices: « Advice » ne se compte pas. Un conseil, c’est « a piece of advice ».

words.eg: The flat came with {furniture} nobody would have chosen.

no.furnitures|a furniture: Jamais de pluriel : « the furniture is old ».

words.eg: There is not enough {information} on that page to decide anything.

no.informations: Indénombrable en anglais, contrairement au français.

words.eg: All our {luggage} fitted in one boot, just about.
The {equipment} arrived a fortnight after the people did.
One {piece of advice}: never sign the first version.
There has been real {progress}, just not where anyone was looking.
{Accommodation} is the single biggest line in anyone’s budget here.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces mots ne se comptent jamais. Lequel se compte ?
odd.why: « A piece of » est précisément le tour qui permet de compter l’incomptable.

words.eg: We {managed to} finish it before the deadline moved again.
He {refused to} put it in writing, which told us everything.
She {offered to} take the early train so we did not have to.
You cannot {avoid} having that conversation for ever.
Somebody {suggested} moving it to a Tuesday.

no.to suggest to do: « Suggest » ne prend jamais l’infinitif : « suggest doing », ou « suggest that we do ».

words.eg: They {promised to} come back with a date and never did.
It is {worth} asking before you assume.

words.en: to remind somebody to do something
words.eg: {Remind} me to send that before I leave.
{Let} me do this bit, you have done enough.

no.to let somebody to do: Après « let », le verbe reste nu : « let me do », jamais « let me to do ».

words.eg: You cannot {make} people care by putting it in a slide.

words.en: to allow somebody to do something
words.eg: They {allow} you to change the date once and once only.

words.en: to expect somebody to do something
words.fr: s’attendre à ce que quelqu’un fasse
words.eg: Nobody {expects} you to know all of it in the first month.
I {spend} more time looking for files than reading them.

words.en: to be used to doing something
words.eg: I am not {used to} driving on that side yet.

words.en: to prevent somebody from doing something
words.eg: Nothing {prevents} you from asking twice.

words.fr: se donner la peine de faire
words.eg: Do not {bother} printing it, nobody reads the paper copy.
By Thursday everyone is {exhausted} and pretending not to be.
words.clue: Un adjectif extrême : on ne dit pas « very exhausted », on dit « absolutely ».

words.eg: It was absolutely {freezing} on the platform.
The garden is {enormous} and entirely made of brambles.
The kitchen is {tiny} and works better than the big one did.
The coffee is {awful} and the company is excellent.
It was {brilliant}, honestly — best thing we did all year.
It is a long walk and entirely {worthwhile}.
The most {annoying} part is that he was right.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces adjectifs sont extrêmes et n’acceptent pas « very ». Lequel est ordinaire ?
odd.why: On peut dire « very worthwhile » ; on ne dit pas « very freezing ».

units.title: Prépositions de lieu et de mouvement

words.eg: The chemist is {opposite} the church, not next to it.

no.in front of: « In front of » veut dire devant, du même côté. En face, de l’autre côté de la rue, c’est « opposite ».

words.eg: Sit {next to} me and I will show you the trick.
Walk {along} the towpath for a mile and it opens out.
The ferry takes you {across} in four minutes.
The path goes {through} the wood and comes out by the pub.
Carry on {past} the bridge and take the second left.
Head {towards} the tower and you cannot get lost.
The view {at the top of} that hill is worth the climb.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces prépositions décrivent un trajet. Laquelle décrit une position ?
odd.why: « Next to » ne bouge pas ; les trois autres traversent.

words.eg: I could {hardly} hear a word over the music.

no.hard: « Hard » veut dire fort ou difficile ; « hardly » veut dire presque pas. Le piège est classique.

words.eg: We {barely} made the last train.
It was {quite} good, which in this country is not a compliment.
It is {rather} colder than the forecast promised.
It got easier {gradually}, and then all at once.
He agreed {reluctantly} and made sure everyone knew it.
{Apparently} it has been like that since the eighties.
The bus was {on time}, which everyone mentioned.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces adverbes disent un degré. Lequel dit un horaire ?
odd.why: « On time » se compare à une heure, pas à une intensité.
